clue.text: Pilot who dreams where some pigeons are heading?

indicators.note: to pilot is to steer, so the following letters are guided into a new course

explanation.surface: A daydreaming aviator is compared with a flock of racing birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pilot' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the anagram signal steering WHO DREAMS into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Homing pigeons fly back to their lofts, the direction of one's own house.

clue.text: I'm surprised leading couple quit play

indicators.note: the front pair of letters leave, as the first couple walk off the stage

parts.note: Shakespeare's tragedy of the Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: A shocked theatregoer reports that the two lead actors walked out of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading couple quit' removes OT from the start of OTHELLO.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of mild astonishment, as in 'Well, what's this?'

clue.text: US subject accepts Queen's Award for Drama

indicators.note: one word takes in another, as a person accepts something handed over

parts.note: Americans call the school subject mathematics math, not maths
the CBE, Commander of the Order of the British Empire, an honour conferred by the monarch

explanation.surface: An American is honoured by the Queen for services to the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US subject' looks like a citizen but is the school subject, spelt the American way without a final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shakespeare tragedy is an example of a stage play.

clue.text: Lift rug running round European hotel

indicators.note: the first word encircles the next, as a border runs round a picture

parts.note: slang for a hairpiece
H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone hoists a carpet that stretches around a continental guesthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rug' is slang for a toupee; 'running round' puts E inside WIG, then H follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors raise an anchor by this verb, so it can mean hoist.

clue.text: Poems lack energy describing mother's heart beats

indicators.note: in crossword usage, describing means drawing a line around, so one part encloses another
the poems are without something, so a letter drops out

parts.note: verses that chime are rhymes
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: the central letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Verses lacking vigour depict a mother's emotional core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is crossword shorthand for drawing round, so the shortened poems word RHYMS encloses the two central letters of 'mother'.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular pulses or patterns of stress, like drumbeats, are this plural noun.

clue.text: Playwright collecting villain's carving

indicators.note: the playwright gathers another word into himself, enclosing it

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw, Irish dramatist
a villain is a crim, short for criminal, so a villain's becomes crim's, the possessive S kept

explanation.surface: A dramatist acquires a criminal's woodwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors' engraving on whalebone or ivory is a traditional decorative art.

clue.text: See 24
German thriller writer's better

parts.note: Eric Ambler, British spy-thriller novelist; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A German spy novelist is described as superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as a comparative adjective but means one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who places wagers is a punter, a crossword-friendly sense of the comparative.

clue.text: Crew perform on string instrument

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
to do a play is to perform it
a line is a length of cord

explanation.surface: A band plays on a stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'string instrument' looks like one phrase, but 'string' gives LINE and 'instrument' alone is the definition: a kitchen slicer.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen tool with an adjustable blade for slicing vegetables thinly, also a spelling of the lute-like mandolin.

clue.text: Dispatch a group of ordinary people across Costa Rica

indicators.note: the laity spread themselves over the country, straddling its abbreviation

parts.note: the laity are those who are not clergy
CR is the international vehicle code for Costa Rica

explanation.surface: Commoners are dispatched across Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatch' is a noun meaning speed, not the verb for sending people off.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatch as a noun means promptness, eager speed.

clue.text: Traveller makes tracks round Arab state

indicators.note: railway letters surround the state

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway
the sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A wanderer heads off around the Gulf nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes tracks' suggests leaving; 'tracks' alone gives RY, surrounding OMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a nomadic people are often called travellers in Britain.

clue.text: Jack hopes to work for old carpenter

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: the letters are set to work, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Jack aspires to employment with a woodworker of long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical husband of Mary was a joiner in Nazareth.

clue.text: Washington's sidekick nearly fools poet

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to have someone, as in 'you've been had', is to fool them, so fools gives has
John Milton, author of Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: George Washington's right-hand man almost dupes a bard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the S from HAS ('fools', as in 'you've been had').
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander, the founding father, served as aide-de-camp to the first US president.

clue.text: Backing group snaffled your drink once!

indicators.note: the group grabs another word and holds it inside
the word for group is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a set is a group
thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: A gang pinched someone's beverage!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns the group word into TES. 'Drink' is slang for the sea, and 'once' signals a prehistoric ocean named after a Titan sea goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-vanished ocean between ancient continents; the sea is often called the drink.

clue.text: Where to take in salty air and a sleep, possibly

definitions.text: Where to take in salty air

indicators.note: the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Advice on a seaside break: sea breezes and a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafront promenade, where people stroll for the sea breeze.

clue.text: Talks about a son and daughter's early years

indicators.note: the talk wraps round the family members

parts.note: says means speaks
a lad is a boy
D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter; 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Chat about a boy and girl when they were young.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion lands after the first letter of the talk word, not in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's phrase for youthful inexperience, now meaning a heyday.

clue.text: Odds on 26 papers like the Globe

parts.note: SP is the starting price, a bookmaker's odds
the answer to 26 across, a star
ID is identification papers

explanation.surface: Betting odds on a star's identity documents resembling a theatre or planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Globe' suggests the theatre; here it is the Earth, a slightly flattened ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earth is not a perfect ball but a slightly squashed round body.

clue.text: Small old coin cracks desirable mirror

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: the coin breaks into the word and sits inside it

parts.note: a plum job is a desirable one
the ecu was a former European currency unit

explanation.surface: A tiny antique coin breaks an attractive looking glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflector in a telescope, or a medical instrument with a reflecting surface.

clue.text: Marx brother tours a grand city

indicators.note: the brother goes round the letters, enclosing them

parts.note: Chico, one of the Marx Brothers comedy team
G is slang for a thousand dollars or pounds

explanation.surface: A comedian travels around a great metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tours' puts A and G inside CHICO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Windy City is a major US metropolis on Lake Michigan.

clue.text: Girl landed up in control of parents

indicators.note: the word sits inside, held by the parents as something in their keeping

parts.note: mum and dad, MA and DA

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: lit, as a bird alighting

explanation.surface: A girl ends up running her mother and father's household, like the Roald Dahl heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the landed word bottom to top, giving TIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, and the Roald Dahl heroine who outsmarts her parents.

clue.text: Wife killed nursing king's evil

indicators.note: holding something within, as a nurse cradles a baby

parts.note: iced is slang for murdered
K is the chess abbreviation for king; 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A wife murdered while tending a monarch's malevolence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing' puts K inside ICED.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness and malevolence are synonyms, adjectives describing great immorality.

clue.text: Revolutionary faction like some tobacco

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist guerrilla
a wing of a party is a faction

explanation.surface: A rebel group resembling a type of smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Some tobacco is chewed rather than smoked, a describing word for that kind.

clue.text: Lapp cut stats about unknown secret publishing

indicators.note: the parts go round the unknown

parts.note: the Sami are the indigenous people of Lapland

indicators.note: the last letter is trimmed off

parts.note: statistics are data
Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A Laplander slashes figures concerning an unidentified underground press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims the stats word to DAT; Z is the algebraic unknown that the other parts wrap round.
explanation.definitionFit: Soviet-era clandestine copying and circulation of banned texts.

clue.text: Soprano cast agree about is fat

indicators.note: the arranged letters go round the soprano
the letters are thrown into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: S is the musical abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: An opera singer and company agree on the matter of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges AGREE to GREAE; 'about' puts S inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal fat or lubricating oil is a noun synonym.

clue.text: Develop primarily loud threatening sound

parts.note: to grow is to develop

indicators.note: only the initial letter is taken

explanation.surface: A noise first becomes loud and menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's deep warning noise in the throat.

clue.text: Rising river swamps women's course

indicators.note: the river engulfs another letter
in a down clue, read upwards, so in reverse

parts.note: the Tees in northern England
W is the abbreviation for women; 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A flooding river inundates a ladies' path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns TEES into SEET; 'swamps' puts W inside. The Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The dessert, one part of a meal, is called a course.

clue.text: Every year top performance pulls in crowd for musical

indicators.note: the outer words draw another inside

parts.note: PA is per annum
an A ... is one's best
a jam is a crush of people

explanation.surface: Every year a great show draws in a crowd for a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'A game' is one's best performance, a sporting idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1954 Broadway show about a pyjama factory strike.

clue.text: Song about working is set on a pedestal

indicators.note: the song goes round the next two parts

parts.note: a Lied is a German art song
on means functioning

explanation.surface: A tune about employment gets idolised.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lied is a German art song, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated as a celebrity and lavishly admired.

clue.text: Star in Fiddler on the Roof

indicators.note: the letters are inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A lead performer in a famous musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'the Roof'.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading figure or celebrity, the protagonist.

clue.text: Sailor shrouded in faint glow at night

indicators.note: the sailor is wrapped inside, as in a sheet

parts.note: slight means faint
tar is an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A seaman wrapped in a weak glimmer after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Light given off by celestial bodies after dark.
